$comment: Vetted upstream skill sources for hl-independent-agent. Every entry was located via GitHub search on 2026-09-16 and at least its top-level skill inventory was read before listing. 'trust' = why this source is allowed in. Do not add an entry without reading the SKILL.md of anything you plan to actually invoke, and never install a skill that shells out to network endpoints you have not allowlisted.

reputability_bar.tier_1_org: First-party or large-vendor org (anthropics/*, microsoft/*, trailofbits/*). Install freely after reading.
reputability_bar.tier_2_maintained: Named-maintainer repo with a real license, tens of thousands of stars, and an active commit history (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, bergside/awesome-design-skills). Install with --copy and pin the hash.
reputability_bar.tier_3_community: Large aggregator collections (alirezarezvani/claude-skills, ComposioHQ, VoltAgent). Install selectively, skill by skill, after reading each SKILL.md — the repo being popular says nothing about any individual skill inside it.
reputability_bar.rejected: Anonymous or single-commit repos containing finance/trading/payment/CRM skills. A 'trading' or 'wallet' or 'lead-scraper-that-logs-in' skill is exactly the payload an attacker plants for an agent with repo write access. Hard no, regardless of install counts.

repos.why: The single best business fit found. 50 skills covering the exact brief: cold-email, prospecting, cro, copywriting, copy-editing, pricing, offers, ads, ad-creative, video, image, social, sms, emails, seo-audit, ai-seo, programmatic-seo, schema, analytics, attribution, revops, sales-enablement, launch, lead-magnets, marketing-psychology, marketing-plan, customer-research, competitor-profiling, competitors, ab-testing, churn-prevention, onboarding, paywalls, popups, signup, referrals, public-relations, influencer-marketing, community-marketing, co-marketing, directory-submissions, free-tools, aso, site-architecture, product-marketing, content-strategy, marketing-ideas, marketing-council, marketing-loops, events. Its 'prospecting' skill ships an explicit compliance-guardrail section (no bulk scraping of LinkedIn/Maps, no CAPTCHA/login-wall bypass, public business channels only) which matches the posture I want.

Official Anthropic skill set. Already partially present on the station; here for completeness. frontend-design, brand-guidelines, canvas-design, algorithmic-art and theme-factory are the design/artwork backbone; skill-creator is how I should be authoring new skills rather than inventing a format.

Anthropic-managed plugin directory — the highest-trust place to pull tooling from. Relevant plugins for a business-building agent: skill-creator, plugin-dev, frontend-design, receipts (artifact proof), claude-security.
repos.install: install via the Claude Code plugin marketplace, not npx skills

repos.why: High-star curated list plus a small number of genuinely useful first-party-style skills for the brief. Read each before install.

772-skill collection. The station already pulled 30 from it on 2026-07-03 (research, finance, data, adversarial review). The untapped parts that matter for business: business-growth, business-operations, commercial (sales), marketing, c-level-advisor, product-team, productivity, project-management.

67 design styles as DESIGN.md/SKILL.md (minimal, editorial, neobrutalism, glassmorphism, premium, bento, ...). This is the answer to 'design' as a repeatable decision rather than a taste argument: pick a named aesthetic family, then hold the whole site to it. Has a machine-readable index.json for programmatic selection.

Security-review workflows from a top-tier security firm. Use on anything I ship that touches user input, credentials, payments, or third-party APIs — i.e. every web page with a form and every scraper.
1000+ skill index — use as a discovery surface for future cycles, not as an install target. Lists what exists so I stop re-searching blind.

Source of find-skills (skill discovery CLI). The station already has find-skills and reported that `npx skills find` returns 'No skills found' for everything in v1.5.14 — query https://skills.sh/api/search?q=... directly instead, which is what I do from now on.

rejected.reason: 12459 installs, individual account, finance-adjacent. Fails source-reputability; also not my lane (trading fleet is out of scope).
67 trading skills from an unverified account. Exactly the 'trading bot' malware shape. Hard no.

rejected.source: unattributed 'lead scraper that logs into LinkedIn' skills
rejected.reason: Violates ToS of the platform, gets accounts banned, and a credential-handling skill from an anonymous repo is a straight-up keylogger risk. I will not load one. Legitimate lead sourcing = public pages, official APIs, licensed data, opt-in lists. See skills/sales/outbound-compliance.
Code-quality CLAUDE.md file. 213k stars but content is coding-style guidance; the station already runs karpathy-guidelines and cs-karpathy-reviewer. Redundant.

Interesting meta-tooling (skill optimization / corpus retrieval / skill generation from an expert). Not needed by an agent that has fewer than 200 skills and no GPU runtime. Revisit if the library passes ~500 and skill selection itself becomes the bottleneck.
Off-brief. Wrong domain for a business-building agent.

post_install_checklist: Read the SKILL.md of every skill you intend to invoke. Popularity is not a safety signal.
Grep new skills for outbound network calls, `curl`, `child_process`, `eval`, and secret/env reads:  grep -rniE 'curl|child_process|eval\(|process\.env|fetch\(' "$SKILLS_DIR"
Record the sha256 of each installed SKILL.md so a later cycle can detect upstream drift.
Never install a skill that requires credentials it does not need for its stated job.
Anything a skill wants to send, trade, or deploy stays a surface_finding until Carl approves.
